name: Spironolactone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Spironolactone raises the risk of high potassium (hyperkalemia), especially with kidney impairment. For heart failure the US label starts 25 mg daily at an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) above 50 and suggests 25 mg every other day at eGFR 30 to 50; it is contraindicated with existing hyperkalemia.

bands.recommendation: Heart failure (K ≤5.0 mEq/L, eGFR >50): 25 mg once daily, may increase to 50 mg (label). Other indications per label.
eGFR >50: as above. eGFR 30–50: consider starting 25 mg every other day (heart failure; label). Monitor potassium closely.
bands.short: HF eGFR 30–50: 25 mg every other day

bands.recommendation: No dosing in label. High hyperkalemia risk: avoid or use with specialist input.
bands.short: No label dose; avoid or specialist

bands.recommendation: No dosing in label. Avoid or use with specialist input.
bands.short: No label dose; avoid or specialist

hd.text: No data in label. In maintenance dialysis, two randomized trials (ACHIEVE, ALCHEMIST; 2025) found that spironolactone 25 mg daily did not reduce cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization, and the updated meta-analysis found no mortality benefit. Do not start it for cardiovascular protection; otherwise avoid or use with specialist input.
hd.short: No CV benefit in RCTs; avoid

monitoring: Serum potassium within 1 week of starting and regularly; kidney function and volume status; contraindicated with hyperkalemia, Addison's disease, eplerenone (label). Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless monitored (label 5.1).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness not established in pediatric patients (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
